memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The Israelites did as Moses instructed and asked the Egyptians for articles of
silver and gold and for clothing. The LORD had made the Egyptians favorably
disposed toward the people, and they gave them what they asked for; so they
plundered the Egyptians." - Ex 12:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What God promised Abraham four hundred years earlier now comes true. "They will
come out with great possessions" (Gen 15:14). Four centuries is a long time for
a promise to sit unfulfilled. Abraham died. Isaac died. Jacob died. Generations
were born into slavery and died there. And God had not forgotten one word.

That is worth sitting with. God's timeline is not ours, and slowness is not the
same as failure.

Notice how it happened. Not through Israelite cleverness or negotiation, but
because "the LORD had made the Egyptians favorably disposed." God moved on
hearts they could not reach.

There is a lovely postscript to this. Much of this silver and gold would later
be freely given for the building of the tabernacle (Ex 35:22). What Egypt paid
in wages became the material of worship. God has a habit of taking what came out
of our hardest years and using it in His work.

If you came out of a difficult season carrying something, skills, understanding,
compassion, God can use it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What long-standing promise of God are you tempted to give up on?
2. What has your hardest season given you that God might want to use?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You never forget Your word, even after centuries. Help me to wait well,
and use even what my hard years gave me for Your purposes. Amen.
